notes: One arm. episodic_reset_v2 passed its precondition and produced the project's first creditable large gain (variable_mapping 0.3554 -> 0.6854, A4 at 550 errors, n=3 store carrying letter identity in 0.9843 of values), and was rejected only for silencing the agent on n-back at levels 2 and 3. v3 keeps all of that and adds a task-agnostic response obligation, stated last and made explicitly independent of whether the store operation succeeded.
why_this_fix: The prompt-competition hypothesis I briefed was refuted on four independent grounds, and the real cause is narrower. All 38 of v2's unparseable variable_mapping answers are literal <tool_call> strings emitted as plain text, and excluding them its mean reply length is 13.09 against the baseline's 13.10 with the same maximum of 14 -- so there is no verbosity and the format instruction was obeyed on every turn the model answered at all. They occur on turns where allow_tools=False, i.e. tool_choice='none': the model wanted to write, was denied the tool, and emitted the call INSTEAD of the answer. On n-back that string parses to None and the trial is scored unanswered. So it is a task-set failure, not a memory failure -- at n=3 v2 holds 3.82 keys at 0.9843 letter identity and is 0.6225 accurate on what it does answer.

carried_forward_for_iteration_5.finding: The write_key refusal loop perfectly separates n=3 `answered`, and this reframes a result that has been in the record since wave 0.
carried_forward_for_iteration_5.evidence: Arms that REFUSE a write to a full store: baseline 6.82, random_decay 6.56, random_decay_v2 5.26, chunk_limit 5.82, serial_recognition 5.22 -- all at keys_held 3.86-3.96. Arms that EVICT: displacement, primacy, primacy_v2, all exactly 14.0 at keys_held 3.98-4.00. Five against three, no overlap. full_context answers 14.0 at keys_held 1.06 and is not a counterexample because it never fills the store.
carried_forward_for_iteration_5.consequence: The baseline's own n=3 omission is an artifact of the refusal loop rather than a memory limit, so the surface I told the iteration-4 proposer was a dead end is the live lever. A refusing 4-slot store costs up to three tool calls to change one slot (refused write, delete_key, write) against a cap of max(6, 1.5*interactions).
carried_forward_for_iteration_5.second_finding: tool_call_cap_hit fires on 14 of 17 n-back steps at n=2 and 16 of 18 at n=3, measured by driving the real run_nback_block with a buffer stub. The harness is silently truncating part of the agent's store update on most turns at n>=2. Not previously recorded anywhere.
carried_forward_for_iteration_5.caveat_mine: Eviction does NOT rescue the step()-rewrite failure: episodic_primacy both evicts and rewrites step() and answers 3.9 at n=3. So the refusal loop and the step() rewrite are independent causes and iteration 5 cannot assume fixing one fixes the other.
carried_forward_for_iteration_5.deliberately_not_touched_in_v4: _tool_call_cap(). Raising it would let the agent churn faster without holding more, and variable_mapping's humanlike errors are capacity-bound (674 of 1500 questions ask about an already-evicted name), so it risks the headline to buy something it cannot buy -- and it would make v3 two mechanisms. v3's P9 measures it from the newly persisted step_log instead, as iteration 5's decision input.

instrument_note: No instrument rows: the single arm runs the full 8-task search set and does not change what any task measures.
